title: Derived pullback along an isomorphism of schemes is the termwise inverse image
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$, with coefficient sheaf $\Lambda_Y$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] equal to the constant sheaf $(A_{E,n})_Y$ for $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and to the completed sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, and similarly on $X$. Let $c_\Lambda:g^{-1}\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$ be the structure isomorphism of the inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]: for $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ it is $c^g_{A_{E,n}}$; for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ it is the composite $g^{-1}\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_mg^{-1}(A_{E,m})_Y\xrightarrow{\varprojlim_mc^g_{A_{E,m}}}\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_X$. Then for every complex $K$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_Y$-modules whose class lies in $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the termwise inverse image $g^{-1}K$, made a complex of $\Lambda_X$-modules through $c_\Lambda$, has its class in $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, and there is an isomorphism
$$
 \lambda_K:Lg^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }g^{-1}K
$$
in $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, natural in $K$, where $Lg^*$ is the derived pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. In particular, for $K=\Lambda_Y$ placed in degree $0$, $\lambda_{\Lambda_Y}:Lg^*\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{-1}\Lambda_Y$.

source.place: node def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology, order 1510 (the canonical Weil structure it names, constructed in def-weil-constant-weil-structure, needs Lg_Y^* on the constant coefficient objects); the analogous identification Lg_s^*N=g_s^{-1}N is used without proof in def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport, item 2. Written by an agent; no document in literature/ states it

proof.text:
Write $F=g^{-1}$. By clauses 1--3 of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], $F$ is relabelling along the covering-preserving site equivalence $\Phi_g$, and it preserves limits and colimits. This description also gives an equivalence of module sheaves over any ring sheaf $R$ on $Y$ with module sheaves over $F R$: relabel the underlying abelian sheaf and its action; relabelling by $\Phi_g^{-1}$ is its inverse, including the action maps. Kernels and cokernels are relabelled, so this equivalence is exact. At finite level use $c^g_{A_{E,n}}$ to identify $F(A_{E,n})_Y$ with $(A_{E,n})_X$. At integral level use the inverse-limit isomorphism in clause 2 and the compatible maps in clause 3 to obtain exactly the ring isomorphism $c_{\mathcal O_E}$ in the statement. For the completed coefficient projections it satisfies
$$\pi_{n,X}c_{\mathcal O_E}=c^g_{A_{E,n}}F(\pi_{n,Y});$$
this follows by composing the defining limit map with its $n$-th projection. Thus restriction of scalars along the projections commutes with this relabelling. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $H^i(FK)\cong F H^i(K)$, naturally, for both coefficient rings. In particular $F$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] it induces the termwise triangulated functor on the ambient derived categories. Lean exactness proof: use the underlying abelian natural comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-module-inverse-image-comparison]; inverse image is an equivalence and hence preserves finite limits and colimits. The faithful exact module-to-abelian-sheaf functor reflects these finite limits and colimits. Restriction along the inverse coefficient isomorphism leaves this underlying functor unchanged. Preservation of binary products gives additivity, which is reflected by the faithful forgetful functor.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; module actions and completed projections relabelled using the site equivalence of lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image

proof.text: For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ the module pullback is $F(-)\otimes_{F\Lambda_Y}\Lambda_X$. Because $c_\Lambda$ is an isomorphism, multiplication $m\otimes a\mapsto a m$ (where the action is transported along $c_\Lambda$) identifies this functor naturally with $F$; its inverse is $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Choose a K-flat resolution $q:P\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The finite-level definition [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] computes $Lg^*K$ by the module pullback of $P$. The displayed multiplication map identifies this representative with $FP$, and $Fq:FP\to FK$ is a quasi-isomorphism by step 1. Their composite defines $\lambda_K$ in the ambient derived category. For naturality, let $T$ be the underived module pullback. The multiplication maps define a natural isomorphism $T\cong F$ on all complexes: for every chain map $u:M\to N$, both paths send $m\otimes a$ to $aF(u)(m)$. Both functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms by step 1 and this isomorphism, so this square descends through the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], in this identified-coefficient case $Lg^*$ is exactly the functor induced by $T$ termwise; its K-flat representative above is identified with $TK$ by $Tq$. The descended multiplication isomorphism is therefore $\lambda$, independently of any functorial choice of resolutions. This also explains the finite-level termwise computation asserted by the definition, rather than using that assertion as a separate theorem.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; finite-level derived pullback on K-flat representatives, followed by the exact-functor computation of Tag 015F

proof.text: Suppose $K\in D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$. For each of its finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves choose the finite locally closed constructible partition in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Its inverse images under the scheme isomorphism $g$ form the corresponding finite partition of $X$. The restriction of $g$ to each inverse-image stratum is an isomorphism onto the original stratum, so the site relabelling of step 1 restricts to that stratum. A covering trivializing the restricted sheaf is relabelled to a covering with the same constant finite module; its stalks have the same finite module values. Hence $F H^i(K)$ is constructible. Step 1 gives $H^i(FK)\cong F H^i(K)$ and introduces no new nonzero degrees. Thus $FK\in D^b_c(X,A_{E,n})$. The subcategories are full, so the ambient natural isomorphism of step 2 is the required one inside $D^b_c$.

proof.text: Put $R_Y=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ and $R_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$, with the coefficient identification from step 1. Apply [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] to $\mathcal O=R_Y$: its natural tensor isomorphism sends a local pure tensor to the corresponding tensor, and its scalar-extension clause applies to every projection $R_Y\to(A_{E,n})_Y$. For complexes, apply the tensor isomorphism to each pair of terms and take the direct sums defining [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The equivalence $F$ preserves these sums by step 1. Naturality identifies both $d_M\otimes1$ and $1\otimes d_N$, and additivity preserves the sign $(-1)^p$. This proves the chain-level tensor comparison $F(M\otimes_{R_Y}N)\cong FM\otimes_{R_X}FN$.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] for the morphism of pro-etale topoi induced by $g$, with source ring $R_Y$, target ring $R_X$, and ring map $c_{\mathcal O_E}$. The small-site universe is that of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the required inverse-image adjunction and finite-limit preservation are given by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and step 1. Module pullback along this ring isomorphism is naturally identified with $F$ by the multiplication maps of step 2, now for $R_Y,R_X$. Hence if $P$ is K-flat with flat terms, the cited preservation theorem says exactly that $FP$ is K-flat with flat terms.

proof.text: Choose $P\to K$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; step 5 makes $FP$ K-flat with flat terms. For $P_n=P\otimes_{R_Y}(A_{E,n})_Y$, the reduction-tower compatibility node identifies $F(P_n)$ with $FP\otimes_{R_X}(A_{E,n})_X$ for every $n$, and identifies the maps $P\to P_n$ and $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ with the corresponding quotient and transition maps for $FP$. Its naturality, together with [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined], gives compatibility under changes of K-flat representative, so the derived reduction towers of $FK$ and $K$ are identified.

proof.text:
For the K-flat representative $P\to K$ with flat terms chosen in step 6 put $B(P)=\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_nP_n$ and
$$C(P)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:B(P)\to B(P))[-1].$$
Here products are the termwise products of module sheaves; they are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] and represent derived products by clause 2 of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence]. With the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $C(P)^j=B(P)^{j-1}\oplus B(P)^j$ and
$$d(y,x)=(-d_By-(1-s)x,d_Bx).$$
Writing $a:P\to B(P)$ for the maps $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, the strict equality $(1-s)a=0$ makes $x\mapsto(0,a(x))$ a chain map $P\to C(P)$. It gives a natural comparison $\eta_K:K\to C(P)$ in the derived category. Apply [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] with the coefficient extension $L=E$: its last sentence identifies precisely this zero-shifted-component comparison with the derived-completeness map, and its isomorphism assertion says that $\eta_K$ is an isomorphism for $K$ derived complete as in [def-weil-derived-complete]. Naturality and independence from the representative are also part of that comparison theorem. This uses the specified strict cone map, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between two Roos-triangle objects.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2, p. 24; L=E specialization of lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison; Stacks Tag 08TC (derived-definition-derived-limit) for the Roos triangle

proof.text:
Use the integral definition [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], to which [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] refers: $Lg^*K$ is represented by the strict cone of the tower $\operatorname{Res}_n g_n^*P_n$. The multiplication isomorphisms of step 2 and the projection square of step 1 identify this tower with $F(\operatorname{Res}_nP_n)$, including its transition maps. The product comparison $F B(P)\cong\prod_nF(\operatorname{Res}_nP_n)$ has $n$-th component $F(\mathrm{pr}_n)$; it therefore identifies $F(1-s)$ with the endomorphism having components $\mathrm{pr}_n-F(t_n)\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$. Applying $F$ to both coordinates of the cone and to the displayed differential in step 7 gives a natural chain isomorphism from $F C(P)$ to that representative of $Lg^*K$. By [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], these comparisons on K-flat representatives descend to a natural isomorphism $\theta_K:Lg^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}F C(P)$, independent of the resolutions. For a derived-complete $K$, define
$$\lambda_K=F(\eta_K)^{-1}\circ\theta_K:Lg^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}FK.$$
The inverse is natural because $\eta$ is natural and all its components on this full subcategory are isomorphisms. Thus this comparison has the required naturality for integral coefficients as well.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; strict cone model and its resolution-independent functorial descent in lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined

proof.text: It remains to put the integral comparison in the stated full subcategory. Apply the triangulated termwise functor of step 1 to a Roos triangle witnessing the derived completeness of $K$ in [def-weil-derived-complete]. By the product identification of step 8 and transition identifications of step 6, and the quotient-arrow identifications of step 6, its image is a Roos triangle for the reduction tower of $FK$, with the required first map from $FK$. Thus $FK$ is derived complete. Step 6 identifies every derived reduction of $FK$ with $F(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$. Step 3 makes these reductions bounded constructible, and step 1 gives the same cohomological vanishing interval as on $Y$. The single interval $[r,s]$ supplied by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] therefore works for every reduction on $X$. These are exactly the two defining conditions of $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Fullness puts the natural isomorphism of step 8 in this subcategory.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2 and the constructible integral category; explicit transport of the defining triangle and the uniform reduction interval

proof.text: Finally the coefficient objects placed in degree zero belong to the relevant constructible categories by clauses 1--2 of [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. Its auxiliary finite-field datum and algebraic closure may be chosen independently of $X$ and $Y$: that statement allows any scheme $Y$ and requires no map from $Y$ to that finite field. Choose a prime $p\ne\ell$, the finite field of size $p$, and an algebraic closure containing the finite extension $E$. This merely instantiates those auxiliary parameters. Specialize the already constructed natural isomorphisms to $K=(A_{E,n})_Y[0]$ and $K=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}[0]$ respectively. The resulting maps are the asserted $\lambda_{\Lambda_Y}$; the coefficient-ring identifications are exactly the maps $c_\Lambda$ fixed in step 1.
